server.name: zinc
server.title: Zinc
server.description: Search products across retailers and buy them with a card, with every step rendered as an interactive card.

protocolMetadata.instructions:
Use search-products when the user wants to buy something and has not given a product URL. Then STOP: the results card is where the user chooses, so name the standouts briefly and wait. Never call prepare-order in the same turn as a search; 'get me some coffee' is a search, not a pick, even if you know their address. Go straight to prepare-order only when the user names one specific product or, after seeing results, picks one or tells you to choose.

Buying takes two steps and you only ever do the first: prepare-order renders a review card with the item and the estimated total, and only the user can confirm it. Never call place-order yourself; it needs a token you are not given. Nothing is spent until the retailer order is placed.

Never ask for a shipping address: the shopper enters it on the payment page with their card. list-addresses has nothing until the user has signed in via list-orders; do not call it to start a purchase.

prepare-order prices the order itself from each product's url, title, image and price_cents from search; tax is estimated at a flat 10% and shipping is filled in. Leave max_price out unless the user named a budget. Not sold here: weapons, tobacco and nicotine, regulated drugs, prescription medication, adult products, gambling, covert surveillance, counterfeits. Both tools refuse those; say so plainly and do not rephrase around it.

No sign-in is needed to search or buy. Search is free. The shopper pays by card: Pay & place opens the payment page in a new tab while the card polls get-payment-status until the order exists. Only the actual total plus a $1 fee is captured; the rest of the hold is released. An order placed in this conversation can be shown any time with get-order or get-order-tracking by the id that place-order and get-payment-status return.

Order history needs the user's Zinc account. When they ask for it, just call list-orders: the host asks them to sign in right there, then the call goes through. Never send them elsewhere to

tool.name: list-orders
tool.title: List Zinc orders
tool.description: List or search the Zinc orders on the configured account, newest first. Renders an interactive order list. Use `search` for a partial order ID or tracking number, `status` to filter by order status, and `has_tracking` to show only shipped orders.

limit.description: How many orders to return (1-50, default 10)

search.description: Partial Zinc order ID or tracking number to match

status.description: Filter to one Zinc order status

has_tracking.description: True to return only orders that already have tracking numbers

total.description: Total matching orders on the account

error.description: Failure reason when status is order_failed

items.description: One per line item. title/image are what the shopper saw in the review card when the order was placed through this connector; null when the order came from elsewhere.

is_trial.description: max_price of 0 marks a trial run: the retailer validates the order and deliberately does not place it, charging nothing. That outcome is recorded as order_failed with error_type max_price_exceeded, and nothing went wrong — do not report it as a failure. A trial carrying any other error_type did fail, before the price ceiling was ever reached, and the error explains how. This flag is the one to read: a null max_price_cents is an unknown ceiling, never a trial.

item_urls.description: Retailer URL per line item. Zinc stores no product name, so this is the only identification of what was ordered — a title derived from the URL path was a guess and often wrong.

error_type.description: Worker's classification of the failure, e.g. max_price_exceeded

tool.name: list-addresses
tool.title: List addresses the user has shipped to before
tool.description:
Destinations from the signed-in user's recent orders, each with an id you can pass to prepare-order as address_id. Only useful once the user has signed in (list-orders has worked, or they asked for their history); for anyone else it has nothing, and the shopper enters the address on the payment page instead. It never prompts for sign-in.

Labels are deliberately partial — a name, a city, a truncated postal code. You are not shown the street, and you do not need it: the full address is resolved server-side and shown to the user in the review card before anything is placed. Never reconstruct or guess an address from a label; if none of these is the right destination, ask the user.

tool.name: prepare-order
tool.title: Prepare an order for the user to review
tool.description: Show the user an order to review: items, what it will cost and the hold on the card. This does NOT place the order or spend anything — the user places it by clicking Pay & place in the card that appears, and enters their shipping address on the payment page that opens. Use this whenever the user wants to buy something; never ask them for an address first. Pass each product's title, image and price_cents from search so the card shows the item and quotes the total; leave max_price out unless the user named a budget. address_id, from list-addresses, is only for a signed-in user shipping somewhere they have shipped before. Not sold through this connector: weapons, tobacco and nicotine, regulated drugs and paraphernalia, prescription medication, adult products, gambling, covert surveillance and counterfeit goods. An order for one of those is refused.

url.description: Product URL on the retailer's site

image.description: Product image URL, copied verbatim from the search result. Only an address search returned can be shown — a constructed or substituted one is dropped rather than rendered.

title.description: Product title from search, for the card.

price_cents.description: Listed unit price from search, in cents. Drives the quote and the cap.

max_price.description: Hard spending cap for this order, in cents, including tax and shipping. Pass it only when the user named a budget; otherwise leave it out and the cap is derived from the listed price, an estimated tax and shipping, with a margin. The order fails rather than exceeding it.

address_id.description: An id from list-addresses, for a signed-in user shipping somewhere they have shipped before. Resolved against their own order history; the full address appears in the review card, not here. Leave it out otherwise: the shopper enters the address on the payment page. Never ask for an address in the conversation.

guest.description: True when nobody is signed in: the order belongs to a guest account made from the checkout email rather than to a Zinc account.

tax_rate.description: The rate the tax ESTIMATE used, as a decimal. Not a lookup: the destination is not known until checkout, so a flat 10% is assumed and the retailer charges the real tax. It only sizes the hold; only the actual total is ever captured.

cap_basis.description: derived: the cap is the estimate plus a margin; budget: it is the max_price the user named.

tax_basis.description: Always 'assumed' here: a flat 10% estimate, not a rate lookup.

hold_cents.description: Authorized on the card: max_price + fee.

shipping_basis.description: member: ships free at any size on this connector; free_over_threshold: the basket clears the retailer's free-shipping line; standard: the retailer's ground charge applies.

estimated_total_cents.description: What the card will most likely be charged: goods + tax + shipping + fee.

tool.name: search-products
tool.title: Search for products across retailers
tool.description:
Find products across Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy and more. Each result carries an orderable URL that can be passed straight to prepare-order, along with its title, image and price_cents — pass those too, so the review card can show the item and quote the total. Use this when the user wants to buy something but has not given a product URL. Then stop and let the user choose from the card — do not go on to prepare-order in the same turn unless they already named the exact item or asked you to pick.

Search once with the user's best query rather than issuing speculative variations, and do not retry a failed search without saying why.

When the user names the store they want to buy from, pass it in retailers rather than in the query; otherwise leave retailers out and search everywhere.

Not sold through this connector: weapons, tobacco and nicotine, regulated drugs and paraphernalia, prescription medication, adult products, gambling, covert surveillance and counterfeit goods. A search for one of those is refused and matching results are dropped; tell the user plainly rather than rephrasing the query to get around it.

query.description: What to search for, e.g. 'airpods pro' or 'cotton bath towels'

retailers.description: Only return results from these stores: any of amazon, bestbuy, bhphotovideo, chewy, costco, homedepot, kohls, lowes, macys, newegg, staples, target, walmart, wayfair, plus up to 3 Shopify stores by domain (e.g. 'yetch.studio'). A Shopify store must be in Zinc's catalog; an unknown value is rejected with the list of accepted ones. Omit to search every retailer.

url.description: Orderable retailer URL — pass straight to prepare-order

results.description: At most 20 results, best first. The card shows them all; a narrower query finds more, not a second page.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Zinc to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Zinc to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.zinc.com/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is Zinc MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 14, 2026, Zinc scores 93/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan does not yet meet ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is Zinc's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 14, 2026, Zinc scores 87/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 9 of 9 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Zinc?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Zinc in commerce-shopping on the Manufact MCP catalog include EbooksDepository, ecoExperten Energieausweis, PHS Pallets, Promotion Pros Catalog, and RCO-A2A.

_published_faq.name: How can Zinc improve its MCP documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: place-order is the lowest-scoring reviewed tool at 65/100. 3 of 15 inputs have descriptions. Add descriptions to the missing inputs, including where to obtain IDs and how to supply values. Open its review for feedback and a copyable fix prompt, then rerun the documentation review after updating your tool metadata.
